rationale: All SIX of my round-1 asks are ADDRESSED — each re-derived at tip 0783a507, none accepted on report. F1 verified by `go doc -all -u ./cmd/mindspec`: claimFailureError and readinessOverrideFailure now each render their OWN doc comment (the comment was moved down to sit directly above func claimFailureError, with a note recording why). F2 verified structurally, not textually: I re-enumerated all 11 production WithPhaseWriteLock call sites at the tip and every one is now covered by the header's 10 entries, INCLUDING the two writers I flagged as missing (advancePhaseOnClaim, EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2); I also confirmed each of the 8 substituted function names exists and is the correct ENCLOSING function for its call site (e.g. ApprovePlan:291 contains plan.go:513; repairPhaseRunE:206 contains repair.go:259). F3 and F4 are function-anchored and the anchors check out. F5 records the discharge with the option taken and correctly states the residue itself remains disclosed-not-fixed. F6 is the strongest fix: the misleading branch is GONE, the 4th parameter removed from sExitContract's signature entirely, both call sites updated, the surviving branch now fires only on freshly-measured dirt (so 'survived materialization' is true whenever it prints), and G6 additionally kebab-cased the WARN and added termsafeEscapeEach at that sink. Health at the tip in my lens: gofmt clean, `go vet ./...` clean, and internal/{complete,next,phase,gitutil} all PASS under -short. I also judged the net-new code in my lens. The G1 attestation design is sound: recordStageMarkerAttestation precedes BOTH PublishStageMarker calls (lines 403/406 and 501/504), the provenance gate runs on BOTH success legs and — correctly — BEFORE the branch advance on the tip==parent leg, so a forged marker can never pull the real ref forward; read failures propagate rather than clearing evidence; and materialize_attestation_test.go covers match / absent / mismatch / read-failure as four separate legs. The G3 renderBDError recovery-line hardening is well-reasoned and safe (strconv.Quote is total over any input, so quoting the raw line rather than the escaped one is fine either way). TWO NEW_ISSUEs, both MINOR, both the same comment-truth class I raised in round 1 — recurring INSIDE the round-1 fix. Neither is a hard block and neither has runtime impact; I am filing REQUEST_CHANGES for consistency with my round-1 standard rather than because the branch is unsafe, and I would flip to APPROVE on either fix OR a reasoned refutation of N1's reading. If the tally authority judges these too small to hold a 12-slot round, recording them as carry-forward items is a legitimate resolution — they are two comment edits and three cross-reference edits, with no code change and no test change implied.
concrete_changes_required: N1 internal/complete/materialize.go:116-123 (recordStageMarkerAttestation's doc comment) — the sentence 'a legitimate crash never demotes its own resume evidence to FOREIGN' is FALSE in the C->D window, and the parenthetical before it enumerates only one of the two crash windows the write-before-publish ordering creates. Trace: the M stage records attestation=C (line 403), publishes marker=C (406), advances the branch to C; the S stage then records attestation=D (line 501) and publishes marker=D (504). A crash BETWEEN 501 and 504 leaves attestation=D with the marker ref still at C and the branch tip at C. On re-run the discriminator reads oid=C, hits the tip==oid leg, and attestedOrClear() compares attested(D) != oid(C) -> clears the C marker and returns foreign -> normal run. That is a legitimate crash demoting its own resume evidence to FOREIGN. The comment's parenthetical only considers 'an attestation without a ref' (the absent-ref case); it misses 'an attestation ahead of the ref' (the ref-at-the-previous-stage case). Note the fix's own TestDiscriminator_MismatchedAttestationForeignClears doc comment already names 'a stale pre-crash value' as a mismatch source — so the shape was anticipated in the test and contradicted in the comment, within the same commit. The BEHAVIOR is correct and fail-safe; only the claim is wrong. Fix: enumerate both crash windows and state the honest guarantee — a crash in the attestation-to-publish window costs the resume (falling back to a fully re-gated normal run), it never admits an unattested resume. Structurally this is the same defect as round-1 F2: a comment drawing a universal conclusion from an incomplete enumeration.

N2 Three branch-authored file:line citations survive the G7 sweep and are stale at the tip. The sweep was complete against the twelve items the round-1 panel NAMED, but it was ask-driven rather than class-driven, so unnamed instances of the same class remain. I classified every surviving `.go:NNN` citation in branch-touched shipped source and docs as branch-new vs pre-existing (by checking whether `git show main:<file>` already contained it); five are branch-new, and three of those five are wrong: (a) cmd/mindspec/repair.go:270 cites 'derive.go:375' for the present-tense claim that bare children-derivation returns 'review' for an all-closed set regardless of a done marker — internal/phase/derive.go:375 is a `const (` block opening the childLifecycle doc comment about `--type task`; (b) internal/approve/plan.go:325 cites 'impl.go:277' as one of the ahead-of-preflight entry points where EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 re-runs — cmd/mindspec/impl.go:277 is `if result.CommitCount > 0 {`; (c) internal/approve/plan.go:499 cites 'derive.go:387' for 'all-open children derive `plan` too' — internal/phase/derive.go:387 is the bare identifier `childEpic` inside a const block. The other two branch-new citations are fine and need no change: internal/hook/hook.go:249's 'cmd/mindspec/instruct_tail.go:30' is ACCURATE (line 30 is exactly the `ctx.DerivationFailed || ctx.Phase == ""` predicate it claims), and internal/phase/phaselock.go:40's 'internal/journal/lock.go:55-61' lands on withReportsLock's doc-comment tail plus its func signature at 61 (the acquire/defer/release body it describes starts at 62) — close enough to find the right thing. Fix: function-anchor the three stale ones, matching what G7 did everywhere it was pointed.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE — the attestation doc comment claims a crash-safety property that the C->D window falsifies
findings.detail: internal/complete/materialize.go:116-123. See N1 for the full trace. The write-before-publish ordering creates TWO crash windows, not one; the comment enumerates only the absent-ref window and then generalizes to 'a legitimate crash never demotes its own resume evidence to FOREIGN'. In the attestation-recorded-but-publish-not-landed window the marker ref sits at the PREVIOUS stage, the attestation names the NEXT one, and attestedOrClear() classifies the legitimate C marker as FOREIGN and clears it. I did NOT execute this window (writing a test would have dirtied the reviewed worktree); the evidence is the code path read end to end, plus the fix's own TestDiscriminator_MismatchedAttestationForeignClears whose doc comment already names 'a stale pre-crash value' as a mismatch source. Behavior is fail-safe and correctly tested — the run degrades to a fully re-gated normal run. The cost of that degradation is worth the fixer re-deriving rather than my asserting: TestBead6Leg_xi_ForeignCommitAfterMaterializationBlocksOnStaleSHA shows that a marker classified FOREIGN once the tip has advanced past the reviewed SHA trips the panel stale-SHA gate, which would make this window cost a tracker-only confirm panel rather than a silent retry. The same question applies to the BRIEF's already-disclosed 'pre-fix in-flight markers classify FOREIGN once post-upgrade (one extra gated run, converges)' residual, which is the same shape. I am not asserting either is worse than disclosed — only that the comment states a guarantee the code does not provide, and the cost estimate rests on the same reading.

findings.title: Net-new G1 attestation and G3 render hardening judged sound
findings.detail: G1: recordStageMarkerAttestation precedes BOTH PublishStageMarker calls with no path around it; the provenance gate is evaluated on both success legs and, on the tip==parent leg, BEFORE AdvanceBranchExpectedOld — so a forged marker cannot pull the real branch ref onto itself, which is the property R6's repro attacked. Attestation read failures propagate and explicitly never clear (materialize_attestation_test.go pins that as its own leg, with a comment saying why). The structural foreign/corrupt/error legs correctly skip the bd read entirely, so the new dependency costs nothing on the paths that do not need it. G3: renderBDError's recovery-line quoting trims leading whitespace before the prefix test, so an indented forgery is caught too; quoting the raw line rather than the escaped one is safe because strconv.Quote is total over arbitrary bytes. No dead code, no swallowed errors, no unused parameters introduced by either.
